title: Pre-Chimera Prep

summary.short: Bin spends the day before the move setting his house, the patrol, and the courier in their right places.
summary.default: The town's agenda from 1.3.a becomes one day of real preparation. Bin checks in with Lily, picks up gear, decides where the family sleeps tonight, and chooses the opening move of the joint hunt before dawn — hunt, fortify, or compromise, depending on what was agreed.

quest.title: Pre-Chimera Prep
quest.summary: Wrap up family, gear, and opening-move choices before the joint hunt.

objectives.label: Pick up a pre-hunt kit at the smith or apothecary
Choose the opening move of the hunt

completionOps.title: Story Sync: Pre-Chimera Prep
completionOps.summary: Bin spent the day before the joint hunt setting his house in order and choosing the opening move.

nodes.text: Frostbitten wakes the way a town wakes when it knows it has a job that day. Doors open earlier. The kettle boils on the first kindling. Children are walked to the school the long way around. Bin sits on the porch of Garr's hut with two cups of tea he does not remember pouring. One steam is still climbing. The other has given up.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Eight hours to the hunt. You have eaten one piece of toast and you have apologized to a chair twice. The system has logged the chair apologies under productivity. I think we are ready. I think we are also not ready. Both can be true. It is the only honest answer this morning.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Three checklists. Family first, then gear, then opening move. If I do them in that order, I keep my head. If I do them in any other order, I think I will trip. Today is a tripping day. Let us not.

nodes.speaker: Lily
nodes.text: You snore exactly the same as before you fell into a portal. I checked. Twice. Once last night for proof, once this morning out of habit. Father said not to wake you. I waited until the second cup steamed. The first cup was my idea of patience.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Patience now has a cup count. Excellent. Sit with me a minute. We have to talk about tonight. The town is going to do a thing, and our house has to do a different thing before the town does its thing. I would like you to be in on the plan.

nodes.prompt: Where does the family sleep tonight?

choices.label: Sleep at the hut, doors barred
choices.summary: Familiar ground, harder to surprise. Garr will not leave it.

ops.text: Family sleeps at the hut tonight.

choices.label: Spend the night under Captain Lysa's roof
choices.summary: Guarded house, full kitchen, three lit windows.

ops.text: Family takes Captain Lysa up on a guest room.

choices.label: Lily and Garr stay in the Mug upper room
choices.summary: Public, loud, hard to follow without being seen. The host insists.

ops.text: Family stays in the Mug upper room.

nodes.speaker: Garr
nodes.text: Hut it is. I will sit in the chair by the door with the lamp on low and a book I do not intend to read. Lily — second floor, west window unlatched in case you need to hand me a tea down through the rafters. Nobody comes through that kitchen door without ringing for me first.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Take the guest room. I will keep three windows lit and a bow under the sideboard. My house is not pretty in a fight but it is honest in one. Lily can pretend to do her schoolwork until I forget to check.

nodes.speaker: Tavern Host
nodes.text: Upper room is yours. The stove in the corner runs all night. I will tell the regulars Lily is my niece and Garr is my old cousin and nobody is to ask follow-up questions on pain of being charged for their own cider.

nodes.speaker: Lily
nodes.text: Brother. You do not have to come home in one piece. You have to come home. Those are different requirements. I will not let father pretend they are the same. Take the long route back if you have to.

nodes.speaker: Bin
nodes.text: Long route. Both pieces accounted for. If I cannot do both, I will choose the second one. I owed you that promise two months ago. I am paying it now with interest.

choices.label: Visit the smith — sharpened blade and a longer poker

ops.text: Picked up smith kit before the hunt.

choices.label: Visit the apothecary — wound packs and a stim

ops.text: Picked up apothecary kit before the hunt.

nodes.text: The smith does not say much. She never does. She tests the edge of Bin's blade on her thumb, frowns, runs it once more across the stone, and hands it back with a poker as long as Bin is tall. 'Bring them back,' she says, and means both the tools and the boy.

The apothecary's shop smells like pine resin and cold mint. Three wound packs in waxed paper, one stim in a glass tube, and a small bag of bitter sugar 'for after, not during.' He warns Bin not to mix the stim with anything proud, then writes the instruction down on the paper anyway because he does not trust pride.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Last call before dawn. The agenda from last night is set, but the opening move is yours. The town will follow whichever doorway you walk through first — that is just how it has been for Garr's family for two generations and I am not going to argue with tradition tonight.

nodes.prompt: Opening move for the joint hunt.

choices.label: Walk Watch Ridge first, push down into Bent Pine
choices.summary: High ground first. Predictable but defensible.

ops.text: Opening move: ridge first, descend into Bent Pine.

choices.label: Two-cell pincer with Peri on overwatch
choices.summary: Two squads converge. Higher coordination cost.

ops.text: Opening move: two-cell pincer with Peri overwatch.

nodes.prompt: Opening move for the quiet watch.

choices.label: Sit the south gate on the next market day
choices.summary: Wait for the courier where they will appear. Patient, public.

ops.text: Opening move: watch the south gate on market day.

choices.label: Stake out the Mug cellar after closing
choices.summary: Quiet, indoor, depends on the host's nerve.

ops.text: Opening move: stake out the Mug cellar after closing.

nodes.prompt: Opening move for the compromise plan.

choices.label: Run the first escorted Bent Pine patrol yourself
choices.summary: Lead from the front so the policy lives or dies on your back.

ops.text: Opening move: lead the first escorted Bent Pine patrol.

choices.label: Open the sealed inquiry envelope with the captain
choices.summary: Names get read out loud — but only to two people.

ops.text: Opening move: open the sealed inquiry with Captain Lysa.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Ridge first. We climb in the dark and we are in position when the trees decide to wake up. I will put two longbows at the saddle and the rest sweep down the spur. You and Peri take the lead — the threat already knows your scent, that is fine, we use it.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Pincer. Risky. We split coordination but we close the back door before it knows to look. Peri runs the overwatch with a horn. If the squads lose contact for more than four minutes, the horn calls a hard reset and everyone runs upslope. No exceptions.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: South gate it is. Two plainclothes on the lane, two regulars at the booth, one of mine in the upstairs window with a horn. If the courier shows, we walk them out polite. If they bolt, we follow at exactly one block of distance. We do not catch them tonight — we map them tonight.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Cellar. Quietest place in the city after midnight. The host gets to be the lookout because nobody questions a tavern host going downstairs at one in the morning. Bin, Peri — you take the back of the trapdoor. If something comes up that should not, the cellar lamp goes out and we collapse the door.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Escort by you. Good. Two guards in front, one behind, you and Peri on the line. The patrol will be slower than your last run. That is the point — slow is what proves the policy works. If you go down, the policy dies the same day. No pressure.

nodes.speaker: Captain Lysa
nodes.text: Sealed envelope. Two pairs of eyes. We read the names, we choose which one we knock on first, and we go to that door in daylight with the writ in hand. Nobody else hears what was in the envelope until the door is open. That is the deal.

Bin tightens the strap on the longest knife he owns and listens to the wind change. Whatever is coming has a rhythm. He has spent two months learning rhythms that did not love him back. This one will not either, but at least it is in his town's tempo. He can move to that. He always could.

Bin double-knots a strap, then unties it because he was rushing. The hands remember more than the head right now and that is fine. The town has loaned him a calmer brain in the form of every door he has walked through today. He will borrow them back at dusk.

nodes.speaker: Garr
nodes.text: Go. Come back. In that order, both required. The chair will be by the door, the kettle will be on the second boil, the dog will pretend not to notice your boots in the mat. I will pretend the same. We are good at pretending. It is half of how this house works.

nodes.speaker: Peri
nodes.text: Chapter 1.4 is closed. The system has logged the family, the gear, and the opening move. The next chapter is the hunt itself, and it gets a fresh canvas. Stand up. Walk through that door first. The town will not move until you do.

nodes.summary: Pre-Chimera Prep filed. Arc 1 hands off to the hunt chapter.

ops.text: Pre-Chimera Prep complete. The next chapter (the joint hunt) opens from the chosen agenda.
